turns.text: Doesn't move. Three heartbeats held under a rib cage in no hurry, four, five — waiting to see whether the gap between turnstiles is worth crossing tonight at all. One eye stays fixed on a ghost-light bleeding in at the corner of sight, an offer that never quite finishes arriving, blinking on a rhythm no blink of the actual eye ever matches.

the platform runs elevated over Ad Plaza's outer ring, rails still slick from the last shower, a monorail's headlamp glow just visible rounding the curve two stops out. underfoot the boards hum faint with track vibration arriving well before any train does. a ticket-scan drone works the far end in slow figure-eights, its scanner-eye painting a thin red grid over every warm shape it crosses, cats included, especially cats. the ghost-light at the eye's edge sharpens for half a second into shape — YOU MAY ALSO LIKE — then dissolves back to nothing, patient, unpaid-for, uninvited.

The red grid means math, not mercy — pattern held, timing counted the same careful way the heartbeats were. Weight tucks in behind a support pillar's cold flank, tail wrapped close, waiting on the exact half-second the scanner-eye turns its back on this stretch of boards.

the figure-eight completes its turn and the drone's scanner-eye swings wide toward the platform's near end, red grid sweeping past a pillar's worth of shadow without catching anything in it. the monorail's headlamp rounds the last curve fully now, brakes exhaling a long metal sigh, windows sliding past lit yellow-white, mostly empty this hour, a handful of tired shapes slumped against the glass. the gap between platform edge and the train's coupling hinges opens for exactly as long as the doors take to cycle.

Doors cycling is a countable thing too. Low sprint along the boards' driest patches, launch timed off the last hiss of brakes, claws catching the coupling's cold housing instead of open air. Wedge in tight where the cars kiss — narrow, dark, smelling of ozone and somebody's dropped noodle carton three stops back.

the coupling gap holds barely enough room, cars grinding a half-inch of play against each other on every curve, wind funneling through in a cold ribbon that smells of brake dust and rain off the rails below. through a sliver of gap, the platform slides away — the drone still working its figure-eight, oblivious, red grid painting empty boards where a shape used to be. the tunnel mouth ahead swallows the last of Ad Plaza's glow whole.

Tunnel dark lands heavy and total, and for once the ghost-light at the eye's corner gutters with it — signal lost, offer unfinished, YOU MAY ALSO LIKE cut off mid-word same as everything else down here. Ears fill the silence the eye used to occupy instead, tracking the wheel-screech's pitch through every turn the tunnel takes.

the tunnel runs longer than the scheduled stop should allow, track lights strobing past too fast to read as anything but a pulse, and for the length of it there's no ad-feed, no scanner-grid, nothing broadcasting anything at all — just wind, wheel-noise, and cold ozone air scrubbed clean of every offer this city usually insists on. it doesn't last. daylight-colored glow starts building at the tunnel's far end, and with it, faint at first, the ghost-light stirs awake again.

That returning flicker registers as a small loss before it even finishes loading, the tunnel's silence already missed the way anything free gets missed the second it's taken back. Braces against the coupling wall as the platform-glow builds ahead, claws finding new purchase for the deceleration everyone else onboard seems to expect.

brakes take hold hard, the coupling's half-inch of play clapping shut and open twice before the whole car shudders still, and Ad Plaza's outer platform slides into view lit up in its full nightly wattage — three stacked drone lanes crossing overhead, a produce stall's heat lamps glowing orange under a tarp two levels down, and from a speaker bolted crooked to a support strut, a bounty broadcast looping flat and corporate: 'KNIFEBOY, LAST SEEN RESTRICTED LOADING DOCK SECTOR, REWARD PENDING VERIFICATION, REPORT ALL SIGHTINGS' — the same six words on a two-second loop, bored of itself before it's even finished.

Six words and a filing tone, same weather as every other broadcast, and it earns exactly the notice it's due — ears flick once toward the speaker, log it, move on. Whatever that name is doing three districts over isn't tonight's business. Slips out through the coupling gap the second the doors cycle wide enough.

clear of the train, the platform's crowd of tired late-shift shapes thins fast toward the stairs, leaving the boards to a produce vendor hosing down crates and a drone lane's steady thrum overhead. past the stall, market stands run three deep under sagging tarps, fish-oil and wet cardboard thick in the air, one stand's overhang torn loose and flapping in a rhythm the wind hasn't quite decided on yet.

Fish-oil wins over everything else in range, worth tracking even with the ghost-light re-flickering its offers across half the visible world now, YOU MAY ALSO LIKE stacking on YOU MAY ALSO LIKE until the eye just stops parsing the words at all. Nose down, weaving stall legs, aimed at wherever the oil-smell pools thickest.

the smell pools under the third stand, where a crate's lid sits loose over trimmed scraps too small to sell — skin, fin, the parts that don't photograph well for the plaza's overhead ad-boards. no scanner reaches this low, no red grid, the vendor two stalls down absorbed in an argument with a delivery manifest that won't reconcile. the crate waits, unguarded, unremarkable, exactly the kind of gap the plaza's whole grid isn't built to notice.

Unremarkable is the best kind of gap there is. Claws hook the crate lid, dragging it aside with a scrape kept as quiet as scraping ever gets, and teeth close on a strip of trimmed skin still cold enough to bite back. Eating happens fast and low, back against the tarp's shadow, ghost-light stuttering its offers over a scene it'll never get paid for.

the vendor's argument resolves somewhere behind, voices dropping to a mutter, and the drone lane overhead cycles its running lights from white to the plaza's default amber-and-teal, marking some shift-change nobody down here needed marked. rain starts again, thin, testing the tarps one drop at a time before committing. the ghost-light flickers once more, a full offer this time — NEKOCORP PLUSH-COLLAR PROMO: SNUGGLE SECURITY BUNDLE, THIS WEEK ONLY — meaningless, unasked-for, gone as fast as it loaded.

A collar promo means nothing chewed, nothing warm, nothing worth the eye's trouble, and gets filed exactly where the bounty broadcast did — noticed, discarded, already fading. What's left of the fish-skin goes down easier than the last bite, and for a moment even the ghost-light's static settles into something closer to quiet.

quiet holds, relatively — the plaza never goes fully silent, drone thrum and rain and a dozen looping ads layered thin enough to blur into one long hum, the kind of noise a body learns to stop hearing as noise at all. under the tarp, dry enough, the crate's shadow makes as good a stretch of ground as any platform offers tonight.

Curl in tight against the crate's cold metal side, tail wrapped over nose, one eye left cracked toward the tarp's flapping edge out of habit more than worry. The ghost-light dims to its lowest setting, an offer left half-loaded, static thinning to something almost like dark.

above the tarp, Ad Plaza keeps its wattage burning regardless, drone lanes trading places on schedule, the bounty broadcast three platforms back still looping its six words to nobody in particular. rain finds its rhythm at last against the market's roofline, steady now, and the plaza logs the night the way it logs every night — mostly, and imperfectly, and without much caring who slept through which part of it.
